passage: Throughout this unit, we have seen that English has traveled farther around the world than any other language.
Along the way, it has become the main tool people use to communicate across borders and cultures.
This spread has produced a huge number of English varieties, which we now call World Englishes.
From British and American English to Australian, South Asian, and African English, each variety reflects the needs of the people who speak it.
English is therefore not owned only by those who learned it as their first language.
It equally belongs to the many people around the world who use it as a second or foreign language.
In this sense, English has truly become everyone's language.
choices: the rules native speakers set for English
